utterances.text: When I use the term "impermissible," I mean that the 4th Detachment was against any arrests, arrests of soldiers, members of the 4th Detachment, and also against arrests of civilians, against lootings, against the appropriation of other people's property, and against everything that infringed upon human dignity.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I believe that -- I can see that it's a map, but this is definitely not what Mr. Pisarevic was intending to use. If I may approach the registrar just for one brief second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] D28/4 ter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pisarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Please, Mr. Antic, would you take a look at this document. Are you familiar with this document? If so, how come, and what do you know about this document?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is the pride of the 4th Detachment. On the 19th of April, via radio, we addressed the citizens of Samac and we put the contents of this document to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please put the document on the ELMO so that the accused in the courtroom can see this.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Is this a document of the command of the 4th Detachment of the Yugoslav People's Army, whose commander you were?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Who drew up this announcement? Who wrote this announcement by which you addressed the citizens of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document reflects the mood that was prevalent at the command of the 4th Detachment. The whole command took part in this. Mr. Zaric was in charge of the style and the wording of the document, and I approved it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Had you not approved this document, this document would not have been published?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, by no means.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you please read who this document is addressed to.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Citizens of Bosanski Samac, Muslims, Serbs, Croats, Yugoslavs, and others.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Muslims, Serbs, Croats. We know who they are. Why is there mention of Yugoslavs following the names of these three ethnic groups?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the ethnic make-up of the 4th Detachment included mainly citizens of Yugoslav conviction, that is, they were members of one of these three ethnic groups, but they considered Yugoslavia as their home and homeland.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: What about these others?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely. It is a well-known fact that in addition to those mentioned so far, there were also Albanians, ethnic Albanians, Roma people, as well as members of other ethnic groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You certainly know that this announcement was published or broadcast in the media and the Bosanski Samac radio station.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. I gave approval for this announcement to be read out publicly over the Bosanski Samac radio station so that everyone gets a chance to learn about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: This announcement reflects the attitude of the command of the 4th Detachment concerning everything that was going on in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This announcement reflects the mood of the command of the 4th Detachment and all its members. We were convinced, however, that it also reflected the views of the vast majority of other citizens who were not members of the 4th Detachment but who accepted the 4th Detachment as such.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: I can see that this announcement is a call to equality, peace, freedom, and equal rights. Were these elements upon which you based your attitude, the JNA and the 4th Detachment, in relation to the different ethnic groups in Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was precisely on these elements that the 4th Detachment was based. The very structure, the very make-up of the 4th Detachment, also reflects this.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: I see here that you condemned nationalists on all sides, and the nationalistic policies. Was that also a faithful reflection of the views of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. What the 4th Detachment believed is that any divisions among citizens along religious or ethnic lines were inadmissible for the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: I've just remembered another question which I wish to ask you. What was the attitude of the parties throughout 1991 and 1992, the SDS, the HDZ, the SDA, towards members of the 4th Detachment and the command of the 4th Detachment? How did they view the very existence of the 4th Detachment of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The command of the 4th Detachment was forced to defend its own legitimacy all the time, again and again. We were under attack from all the different national parties, the SDA and the HDZ, for the reason that Muslims and Croats were members of the detachment. And the SDS attacked us because we were a mixed detachment, including all the different ethnic groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Which means that you did not enjoy the support of any of the nationalist parties, then?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's precise. None of the nationalist [as interpreted] parties liked us.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Objection for the transcript and for the translation. This witness said "national parties," and we heard -- and we have in the transcript, we have another word, "nationalist." So it's just a correction to the interpretation. Because the witness said "national parties," not "nationalist." So ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pisarevic can correct that with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Page 47, all should be redacted. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you say that those were the views of the national parties or nationalistic parties?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said national parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Any other corrections to be made? The question which I asked was incorrectly reflected in the transcript. I said towards the end of 1991 and in 1992, what was their attitude or their view? You spoke about 1992.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I spoke about 1992, as far as the establishment of the 4th Detachment is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. The members of the command - I will no longer be needing this document, thank you - what were the consequences for members of the command after this document was published in the media and over the Samac radio?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After this announcement by the 4th Detachment was published, and after what had gone on before that, very difficult times followed for the command of the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: What happened to the members of the command of the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the announcement was published, my friends let me know that one of the volunteers was looking for me about town, one of the volunteers from Serbia, known as Lugar. His real name was Slobodan Miljkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: What did you do then?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The thing struck me as strange, but I was not surprised, in view of my views and attitudes that were well known, in view of the way things had developed. I made a decision, on my own, to speak the next day - I think it was a Tuesday, the 21st or the 22nd - to the commander of the police station and to ask what the whole thing was about and whether I could count on his protection.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us who the commander was of the police station. And did you actually go to see the commander, and what happened there?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the police - his office was at the department store - when I told him about this, there was very soon a phone call. He merely said "yes." In the meantime, he told me that he could offer no protection, and then Slobodan Miljkovic, in a very energetic manner, entered his office. That was the first time I met him, and the first thing he did, he hit me on the face. He broke my temple bone. He insulted me. He maltreated me. He called me a communist. He said: You're the commander of a communist detachment. We'll make sure you remember us. And so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Pisarevic. The witness didn't actually answer your question as to who the commander of the police was. I mean, I think we know, but I think we need the witness to answer that directly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The police commander was Savo Cancarevic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel's microphone please be turned on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what happened after that?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was badly beaten and I was disarmed. I was put into a passenger vehicle, escorted by three volunteers. They took me to a place I didn't know. We reached a forest eventually, known as Arandzicka. Lugar, who was driving, pulled over. He pulled down the window, and a man appeared through the window into the car. He was wearing a police cap. I recognised Stevan Todorovic. He told me: Oh, it's you. After that, they exchanged some whispered remarks and then we continued our journey.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Where did they take you?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They took me to the village of Obudovac. They told me that this was a prison. They locked me up in some sort of a toilet and left me there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: How long did you stay there locked up like that in the toilet?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stayed there for a day, and then a messenger came and said that they would take me back to Samac. When I returned to Samac, I immediately went to the command. I informed the command what had happened to me. I informed the command about what had happened to me, but not only to me, also Mr. Zaric [Realtime transcript read in error "Todorovic"] told about his own experience at the police station, something he suffered on the hands of another volunteer. He told us --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: One correction for the transcript. Also Mr. Zaric told about his own experience. Here it says "Mr. Todorovic," on page 50, line 16.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. It will be corrected. Because we heard the name Zaric in the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you proceed, please? What did Mr. Zaric tell you?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the command, Mr. Zaric spoke about his own experience, that he was being threatened, that a gun had been put into his mouth. Naturally, everyone at the command was taken aback by this sort of behaviour, the way members of the command were being treated. So naturally, we informed our superior commander about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Let us just clarify this. Did Mr. Zaric tell you about his own experience before you had the incident at the police station?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I had already spent a day at the prison in Obudovac, Mr. Zaric told me at the command, he told me and he told all the other members of the command.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Who took you back from Obudovac?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A volunteer from Serbia took me back. He drove me back to Samac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Pisarevic. Mr. Antic didn't actually answer your question as to when Mr. Zaric told Mr. Antic about the experience with the gun in the mouth and so on. Was it before what occurred to Mr. Antic had taken place or was it subsequent thereto.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: You heard all this, Mr. Antic, and my question. Can you please answer that question. Were you informed by Mr. Zaric about his own experience prior to your own experience at the police station?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I personally heard this at the command.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Was that before your own experience? We are not doubting the fact that you heard this at the command, but was that before you had your own experience at the police station or after that?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: May counsel please be asked to speak into the microphone, for the sake of the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: If you can remember.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I can't remember. Essentially, what I told you is what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: What did you do then? What steps did you take after you informed the commander of the 17th Tactical Group?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Naturally, as a human being, and as commander, I could not accept that. That was why I left, or rather, I told the command, when we were informing each other, that I couldn't accept that, that I couldn't bear that, and that most probably I would resign as commander of the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: What did members of the command tell you then?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In addition to being very sad about it, they had a hard time accepting it. They pleaded with me to stay in my position as the commander of the 4th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: So what did you do then?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Despite all, I couldn't take the humiliation. I went to the command of the 17th Tactical Group the next day. I told the commander about everything that had happened and I resigned.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: What did the commander do then, after he heard your story and your reasons? Did he try to convince you to stay?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The commander of the 17th Tactical Group tried to persuade me to stay, tried to convince me to continue in carrying out the tasks and aims of the 4th Detachment, but I remained adamant.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: So what was his final decision?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He accepted my irrevocable resignation and he passed an order appointing my deputy, Jovo Savic, as commander. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, I'm not objecting. Could we get a date, if possible, on this resignation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pisarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please give us the date when you stopped being commander of the 4th Detachment and when this duty was taken over by Captain Jovo Savic.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this was the 23rd of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: What did you do after that? Where were you assigned? To which unit? And what tasks were you given?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, as an officer, I put myself at the disposal of the command of the 4th Detachment. As I was an expert in defence lines, I was given the task to secure the line that was taken on the embankments on the Bosna and Sava rivers, or rather, to place concrete bunkers there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please clarify this a bit. Where did you place these bunkers? Who worked on the placement of these bunkers? And generally speaking, on carrying out this task.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 4th Detachment wanted very much to make this line safe for its members who were guarding that line, and that is why they decided to establish such facilities from the bridge on the Sava, along the right bank of the Sava River, to the mouth of the Bosna River, and along the embankment of the -- along the Bosna River. So as I was carrying out this engineering work, I made about 60 bunkers. Can I proceed? In order to carry out this work, I got appropriate mechanical equipment and an appropriate labour force. As far as mechanical equipment is concerned, I got two diggers. A Serb worked on one of these, because before the war, he had had diggers in his own company. As for the other digger, I can give you the name of the other person who operated that. This other digger operators name was Bogdanovic Predrag [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter cannot hear the counsel Pisarevic.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the other digger, a Croat was operating it, Tomislav Nenadic. I think that is his name. He was an ethnic Croat.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Just one correction. I believe that I heard the name of the previous one, Goranovic Predrag, and here it says Bogdanovic Predrag. It's on page 54, line 6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Counsel can --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Counsel can correct that and --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And Mr. Pisarevic, remember to wait for the -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Would you just pause for a second. What was the name of the person who operated the digger?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The name of the person who operated the digger was Predrag Goranovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: What about the other person?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter cannot hear Mr. Pisarevic again.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The other person was Nenadic. I think his first name is Tomislav. He is an ethnic Croat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pisarevic, make sure that you're speaking close to your microphone. Twice the interpreters haven't been able to hear what you're asking the witness. And also avoid overlapping the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly. I'll do my best.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: You said that this other person was Tomislav Nenadic, an ethnic Croat. Did he work with this construction machinery before as well?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The man who operated that machine before the war, in his own company, worked with that very same machine.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: The third person?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The third person who worked with this equipment, actually, with the fork equipment, was a Muslim. His last name was Dumonjic. And before the war, in his company, Mebos, he operated the same kind of equipment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Try to describe this briefly to us. What did this -- how was the bunker made? What did other people do? Just do it nice and slowly, please.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are concrete bunkers that fall within the establishment, and they were built in a construction company that made such goods even previously, that is to say, such construction equipment. The forklift brought these elements in, or rather, four concrete elements were required to build a bunker.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pisarevic, we don't need these details. I think the interest for this Trial Chamber is to find out the labour force, who were the labour force, where did they come from, in view of the work obligations issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: In addition to the equipment, there were also a labour force?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: How many were there? What were they by ethnic background, and how did they come to carry out these duties?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The labour force for carrying out this work was assigned by the secretariat for National Defence, and through Dzemal Kapetanovic, their own employee, they assigned a maximum of up to ten people, who were involved in this technical work. The work that they did consisted of the following: They would keep holding these elements until the forklift placed them in an appropriate position. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, just on that issue that the President of the Chamber just raised.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Regarding the concrete. Of course the method of construction and so on is not important. That's not the significant thing. But there has been some evidence in the case regarding who made the concrete pieces for use later in the bunkers, and I don't know, but the Chamber may be interested in that, or it might be of significance to Mr. Pisarevic. I don't know. But I just raise that for your attention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. That can be -- the witness can give evidence on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The witness said that these concrete elements were made by a company that was involved in the building of these concrete elements before the war too. Of course, before the war crimes they were not used for bunkers, but they worked on concrete --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters cannot follow this, because both speakers are speaking at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: When this kind of work is carried out, what was the degree of security provided for you personally and for the people who were engaged in this work?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, since the work was being carried out at the defence line itself, there was the danger of wounding, either by small arms on the other side of the Sava River or from a mortar shell. I personally, as I supervised these operations, I made sure that nothing happened to any one of these men. As soon as I would hear a shell flying through the air, they would have to go into the shelter and I would be the last person to go in.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Did it ever happen that anyone, while these operations were being carried out, the ones that you supervised, did anyone ever get wounded or was anyone ever hurt in any way?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These operations went on for about a month, and throughout this time, not a single worker sustained even a minor scratch.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you just tell us what the ethnic background was of the other auxiliary workers, so to speak, in addition to the digger operators, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. After that, what did you do? You said that this went on for a month.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: When you finished this work, what did you do then, in the units of the army of Republika Srpska, which was already established by then?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When this work was completed, successfully so, there was a high degree of security and safety for all the persons involved. The command sent me to assist the military medical units at the line in the village of Grebnice, where I drove a van, where I got the wounded out of the trenches, took them by ambulance, by this van, to the village of Donja Slatina, where the medical centre was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know about anything related to the crime that was committed in the village of Crkvina? When did this happen? Who did it?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know about these events, about the unheard of crime that was committed in the village of Crkvina. I was there where the facilities were being built, and we heard about it, because people were talking about this at the line. They were saying that this crime had been committed. And it was said that this was carried out by the same person who had maltreated me, and that is Slobodan Miljkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know when the army of Republika Srpska was established?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The army of Republika Srpska was established on the 12th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you know when the Yugoslav People's Army left the territory of the 17th Tactical Group, or rather, the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that the Yugoslav People's Army left the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina on the 19th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: What kind of military units were established then in the territory of the municipality of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In view of the situation, that is, that the army of Republika Srpska was being established and that the Yugoslav People's Army was departing, a reorganisation was carried out, a reorganisation of units. Instead of the 17th Tactical Group, the 2nd Posavina Brigade was established, and the 4th Detachment was reorganised, and it grew into the 5th Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you know at which localities in the town of Samac there were persons who were detained?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know the persons were detained in the police station, at the Territorial Defence headquarters, at the gym of the high school, where I had worked for a long time, and in the remains of the elementary school, because the elementary school had burned down but the gym was left, so they were kept at the gym.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know who was appointed commander of the 2nd Posavina Infantry Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Colonel Mico Djurdjevic was appointed commander of the 2nd Posavina Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you know how long he stayed in that position?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He stayed in that position for a very short time. I'm not familiar with the reasons why he stayed in the position of commander for only seven days.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who replaced him as the commander of the 2nd Posavina Infantry Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he was replaced as commander of the 2nd Posavina Brigade by Dragan Djordjevic, also known as Crni.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who was appointed chief of the brigade?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Another volunteer was appointed to that position, a volunteer from Serbia. His name was Srecko Radovanovic, nicknamed Debeli.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: They were both members of the group that had arrived --

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: They were, to all intents and purposes, your commanders too at that time, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: After your involvement with the medical unit, what was your next assignment? What else did you do in the army?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After that duty, which lasted for about two months, out of my own personal revolt, which was my natural reaction to what was going on, I left and went to stand guard at night in a bunker, as a common soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: How long did you stay there?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For about eight months.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: When peace was finally brokered in Bosnia-Herzegovina, which position did you hold?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some people understood that I was not to be kept in the trenches, being an officer, and I was transferred to another unit for anti-tank defence, anti-armour defence, in the village of Obudovac I was appointed assistant commander for morale.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And that was the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this concludes my examination-in-chief. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krgovic. MR. DI FAZIO: Your Honours, can I just very briefly raise a matter of procedure with you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Before Mr. Krgovic starts his cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: You recall that yesterday we had the issue arise of you wanting to know the Prosecution's attitude towards the 92 bis statement of Mr. Ramusovic, and -- would Your Honours just bear with me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: And we indicated -- you indicated that you wanted to hear from us today. Do you want to do that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Since you're already on your feet, can you just go ahead. MR. DI FAZIO: Well, Mr. Weiner is going to do it, and that's the only reason I ask, so that he can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Let him do it. Let's have it done. MR. DI FAZIO: Let's have it done. Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the statement appears to satisfy the 92 bis requirements. We only have two objections to it. In paragraph 17, the last sentence of the paragraph: "This generally disturbed all citizens because nothing like this had ever happened in Samac." This is his personal opinion. There's no indication that he took any sort of poll or went out and polled citizens or there was any vote. It's strictly his opinion and should be stricken. And also in paragraph 24, there's some discussion of a family feud. It's our argument -- that's the last two sentences, or -- pretty much, pretty much most of the paragraph concerns a family feud. It's not relevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The whole of paragraph 24?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No. Just after - let's see - after the second sentence, it's all family feud. I don't feel it's relevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can you just spell out the beginning of the words of the part which you object to?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: "My brothers, except Izet, also visited me. Izet never came to see me. He was an SDA member when I was wounded."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The rest of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That's all. That portion there. It's not relevant, in our opinion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We shall take our break for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pisarevic. Oh, sorry. It was Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Antic. My name is Dragan Krgovic. I'm speaking here on behalf of Mr. Tadic's defence. I will ask you a number of questions related to the answers you gave Mr. Pisarevic. You answered Mr. Pisarevic's questions about the make-up of the 4th Detachment, and you said that Miroslav Tadic was assistant commander of the 4th Detachment for logistics; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: In your answers to Mr. Pisarevic, you have described the way in which the 4th Detachment was armed, how weapons were signed for, and how equipment was signed for. In view of your explanations, I'm inclined to conclude that Miroslav Tadic, as assistant commander for logistics and in view of the situation that you had no warehouse and no proper logistics, his logistics unit did not actually take part in this arming, did it?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. Mr. Miroslav Tadic, as assistant commander for logistics, in terms of arming the 4th Detachment, as this was done from the warehouse of the 17th Tactical Group, Miroslav Tadic had no specific duties in relation to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Antic, you have described your movements during the night between the 16th and 17th of April. You told Mr. Pisarevic that in the morning of the 17th, you went back to the command of the 4th Detachment from Pelagicevo. Did you say that?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember Miroslav Tadic reporting to the command, asking whether he needed to be involved and whether he should come on the same day? Do you remember that you told him that there was no need for him to be involved for the time being and that he would be called upon when necessary?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Krgovic, don't give the answers to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I am merely stating the view of my client, what he said during his examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, but you're asking this witness. Let him say what happened or what he knows.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, please, Mr. Antic: What happened when you came back on the 17th?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I ordered the duty officer at the command of the 4th Detachment to inform all members of the command of the 4th Detachment about that, when we reached the command of the 4th Detachment, which was at the Sit company building, we were all there together, members of the command, but I remember that Mr. Tadic, assistant commander for logistics, reported and asked whether his presence was required. Given that the operational section of the command had to be there, had to be present, I told him that he was not needed at that moment, that his presence was not required.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Antic, the next day, did you issue any order to Mr. Tadic in addition to the one you spoke about on controlling the collection of weapons? Did you issue Mr. Tadic any other orders?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the next day, the 18th of April, the assistant commander for logistics had some specific tasks in addition to the tasks that he had already been given concerning collection of weapons, he was given another specific task, namely, for the command post to be moved to a different location, which means that equipment had to be taken care of and moved to the new location so the command post could move there and continue operating. Furthermore, I ordered him to set up a kitchen for the 4th Detachment, which he did, as ordered.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Antic, where was this kitchen set up?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The kitchen was set up on the premises of the Tekstilac company, which is adjacent to the Sit company. Prior to these events, there had been a kitchen there, a big one, for the employees of that company.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Antic, was that the only kitchen set up by Mr. Miroslav Tadic that you had ordered?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was the only order that I gave him in terms of setting up kitchens.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Antic, can you tell me, please: The same day, on the 23rd of April, when you ceased to be commander of the 4th Detachment, do you know that Miroslav Tadic also left the 4th Detachment and assumed another position?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He did take up a new position, a different position, but the only thing I'm not sure about is whether it was on the very same day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Antic, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic? MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, just one -- before Mr. Pantelic starts. There's a slight ambiguity that may be important. The last question asked by Mr. Krgovic -- I'm sorry. I withdraw that objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honours. I do apologise. I just have to, for a second, to organise my papers. Thank you for your understanding, Your Honours

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Antic. My name is Pantelic. I defend Mr. Blagoje Simic. Can you please tell me: You know Dr. Blagoje Simic, don't you?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: How long have you known him for, as you were a teacher? Do you know him from your days at school?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not from that period, but I met him when he came to work as a doctor in Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Antic, how do you see Mr. Blagoje Simic as a man, as a human being? You did live in the same town, after all. Just very briefly, your personal view.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was only very seldom that I was in a position to talk to him personally. I do know that he worked as a physician. In a small town like Samac, all doctors, all physicians, are some sort of authority.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Was he a riotous person or an indecent person? You were after all chief of police in Samac at that time. What would you say about his behaviour as a citizen in his spare time? I'm not talking about him as a professional now? MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: The witness has said that he doesn't know him. He came to -- he knew him -- when he came to live -- work in the town as a doctor, saw him in a position to talk to him personally. So we've got no -- he can't provide an answer to that particular question, I would have thought.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. With regard to his character.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honours -- MR. DI FAZIO: Unless the question is directed to some sort of public persona of Dr. Blagoje Simic. Then I would have no objection. But it's got to be clearer, and the way it stands at the moment, that aspect is not very clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I mean, let me explain the way why I would like to have personal knowledge of this witness of behave of Dr. Blagoje Simic. Because he lived in the same town. It's not New York city, it's not Tokyo, not Paris. He says he doesn't know him as a pupil, as a student, but when he came as a physician in the town he made some contacts. Just briefly I would like to explore this matter, because this witness is a former chief of police in Samac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Antic let's neglect this debate with the Prosecution. In his free time, what do you know about Blagoje Simic? Did he go to pubs? Did he spend nights on the tiles? Was he a loud person?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Mr. Blagoje Simic is an intellectual. I was not informed that he displayed any kind of indecent or riotous behaviour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You were a person with a lot of experience, teaching experience, but also a man who held certain posts and offices. In the former system you were chief of police in Samac. You had completed the military school for reserve officers. You attended a number of military trainings and exercises in peacetime. You will, I hope, agree with me if I say that you're a person with an above-average knowledge of military theory and practice, but also as concerns police work. Do you agree with me on that?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is out of modesty only that I would call my knowledge and my skills average merely.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I fully understand that, but you did organise a number of military drills prior to 1992, during peacetime, in Samac?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not personally organise those military drills. It was done by the command of the TO staff. I was an officer at that command. My last duty at the TO staff was assistant commander of the municipal staff for morale.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Antic. We'll take your modesty into account. I think that's beyond suspicion. But your knowledge was still above that of an average soldier, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You certainly knew more than an average policeman, because you were, after all, chief of police, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: You will agree with me - I'm a layperson myself, but please correct me if I'm wrong - in the army, there is a doctrine that's still applied, even nowadays, a principle, I think Mr. Pisarevic asked you about that, the principle, namely, of subordination.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In all the armies of the world there are some principles which are accepted all over the place. That's singleness of command and subordination. There's a man who issues orders, but then up the chain of command, he is subordinated and responsible to his superior officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: As concerns the police forces, was there a hierarchy there too? First comes the municipal police station, and who is above them? Can you just tell us very briefly, please.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can explain this from the way it was organised in peacetime. The secretariat of the interior was responsible for its work up the chain of command to the public security station, established at regional level, and then down the same chain of command, further upwards, to the republican Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Just one small correction. It's a matter of accuracy of the transcript. On page 69, line 18. The witness was referring to the public security centre established at regional level. The station is in the municipality. Then there is the regional centre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I think the witness can correct that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understood you perfectly, your explanation. But for the sake of the transcript, we need to deal with this. So we're talking about the local police station. So who was above that?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The public security station at regional level. More specifically in the case of Samac, it was based in Doboj. And then the republican secretariat of the interior at republic level.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: My apologies, Mr. Antic. There is no luck with the transcript today. Can you tell us: What is the lowest level in this chain of command of the police? What is the lowest level?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The municipal secretary of the interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What comes next above the municipal secretariat?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Public security centre at regional level.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In the case of Samac municipality, who was the superior?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Doboj public security centre. It was based in Doboj.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And then above the Doboj regional centre?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Above the Doboj regional centre, there was the republican body of the interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I hope we've got this clarified now. The first time around you gave an accurate answer, but -- [In English] I see my learned friend on his feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: My problem, just as far as the full clarity is concerned, I assume that the witness is talking of this chain of command that existed pre --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: In peacetime. MR. DI FAZIO: I'm sorry. I missed that. In that case, I'm sorry for my interjection.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That's beyond dispute. That was in peacetime. Can you please tell me, in terms of this hierarchy or chain of command: What was it like during the war, in the Republika Srpska? What was the hierarchy like, in terms of the municipal station and then the region, the level above? Were there any differences? Tell us, please, if you know.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the war, instead of Doboj, as public security centre, I think Samac was subordinated to the centre in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And then above Bijeljina, who was above Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The republican level.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Antic. The 17th Tactical Group had about five detachments, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell the Court: How many military conscripts all together were under the command of the 17th Tactical Group, if you can remember, please? These five detachments, how many people did they include?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This should be calculated according to the establishment, how many. The 4th Detachment numbered about 450 men. Therefore, the remaining four detachments, about as many, I suppose. So there you have the overall number of conscripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: As part of the 17th Tactical Group, was there also an armoured battalion or an armoured brigade?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I'm not particularly familiar with the structure of that unit. I'm an infantryman myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us what kind of weapons the 17th Tactical Group had. Just an example. I'm not talking about numbers. Can you please tell us generally about the weapons at the disposal of the 17th Tactical Group. Did they have any Zoljas, hand-held rocket launchers? Did they have any tanks, did they have automatic weapons? I mean, you are a high-ranking officer.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the 17th Tactical Group had all those weapons that you refer to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: In fact, Mr. Pantelic, we've got this evidence already from one of the earlier witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: If it's not in dispute, no problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It's already on record with our evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. I agree. Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Antic, can you tell me, please: Do you have any personal information on the atmosphere prior to mid-April 1992? I'm talking about February and March, in the villages surrounding Samac, in Prud and so on and so forth. Specifically, what I want to know is: Do you have any information concerning certain military structures of Croats in the surroundings of Samac, and did you perhaps personally witness people arming themselves? Were people digging bunkers or anything along these lines? Your personal experience, please. Tell us briefly.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to our intelligence information, we did have information that, in the village of Prud, there was a unit of the Croatian Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell me, Mr. Antic: What was your information, your knowledge, as commander of the 4th Detachment, concerning the movements by enemy groups in the surroundings of Samac? What I want to know specifically: Prior to mid-April 1992, several weeks earlier, did you have any knowledge or information concerning a possible attack on Samac? If so, please tell us the source. And if you knew about the attack, who, what were you told the attack have come from? Please, only your personal information.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I received the order of the commander to position the 4th Detachment at the defence line within my area of responsibility, my personal assumption was, and the first thought that came to my mind, was -- MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: No objection to this line of questioning, as long as the witness is not talking about his assumptions, but his direct knowledge. It's important for you to know that, and important for him to speak of what he knows, what he heard, what he saw and observed, not his own conclusions or assumptions or opinions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Antic, let us perhaps subdivide this subject into a few. During March and the first half of April, do you know about the formation of some kind of Crisis Staff of the HDZ and the SDA in Samac? Did you have any information about that?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no knowledge about any such thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Tell me: What is your personal knowledge regarding possible attacks against Samac before the 16th of April, 1992? Do you have any knowledge about that?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have any knowledge. But one of my men, just before the conflicts between the 16th and the 17th, told me personally that there was an enormous concentration of the military in the area of Slavonski Samac, because he had passed there and seen it for himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Could you please be so kind as to tell me the name of the man who told you that, and also when he told you that.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: His name is Diko Simic, and he told me about seven days before these events.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So around the 10th of April?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: At the level of the 4th Detachment, at the level of the command of the 4th Detachment, did you discuss that particular piece of information that major troops were being built up in the area of Slavonski Samac?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we didn't discuss that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did you personally perhaps discuss this at the level of the 17th Tactical Group?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every meeting with our Superior Command that we had, we always discussed these events and we always presented information about everything. So I conveyed this piece of information that I had to my commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That was Lieutenant Colonel Stevan Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And at the level of the command of the 17th Tactical Group, this information was discussed, I assume.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: All right. Tell me, please, Mr. Antic -- let me just have a look. Mr. Antic, did you have any personal knowledge about the plebiscite of the Serb people in Bosnia-Herzegovina and the topic of this plebiscite? Did you personally take part in it?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am aware of the plebiscite. It had to do with stating our views on whether we wanted to live in Yugoslavia. I personally did take part in this plebiscite.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you happen to know from the newspapers, or on the basis of your personal knowledge, what the outcome was?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A vast percentage voted in favour of a life together.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In January and February 1992, did you personally hear that the Republika Srpska was established, or rather, at that time the republic of the Serb people in Bosnia-Herzegovina? Did you know about that?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was a well-known thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did you know that sometime around then, the constitution of Republika Srpska had been passed?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is logical. When a decision is reached, then it should be translated into law.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Since you said that the army of Republika Srpska was established on the 12th of May, 1992, do you happen to know when the ministries of Republika Srpska were established? I'm specifically interested in the Ministry of the Interior, when it was established. If you know.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about those dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Tell me, Mr. Antic: You spoke about a meeting on the 16th of April that was attended by your assistant commander for intelligence and security matters, Mr. Zaric. This was in the local commune in town; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you remember having said that to my colleague Mr. Pisarevic by way of an answer?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Do you know that in the town of Samac, that is to say, in the local commune in town - I'm not referring to the villages now - that a Crisis Staff had been established by the inhabitants there, the members of various political parties, in order to ease tensions? Did you know about that? Specifically, what meeting had he come from? Was that a meeting of the Crisis Staff of the local commune in town?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This was no Crisis Staff meeting. This was a meeting of the representatives of political parties only. They presented some of their own requests, and the radical request related to the 4th Detachment. Our representative did not have the authority to make such a decision, or could he have made such a decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: All right. But if Mr. Zaric says that such a Crisis Staff did exist within the ranks of the Croats and Muslims, you would have no doubt -- no reason to doubt that, because he's a man who is well informed?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'd have no reason to doubt that, but this is what I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: All right. Tell me -- oh, yes, yes. Oh, the 4th Detachment. Yes, that's what we're discussing. Let me just find this. Yes. Within the 4th Detachment, tell me, Mr. Antic: How many companies were there? So lower-level units, right? How many were there?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Four companies.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I'm a layman, so I don't know whether we are talking about unit leader or a unit commander.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unit leader.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: All right. The leader of the 1st company, was that Milan Celikovic?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And the leader of the 4th company, was that Milan Vujic?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So who was it?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Milan Vujic was --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Oh, leave aside Milan Vujic. Do you know who the leader was?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rajko Dragic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And who headed the 2nd Company?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dzemal Jasenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And who headed the 3rd Company?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ramusovic, and I think his first name was Naser.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: All right. And who was commander of the Scout Squad within your 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: By its very establishment, the 4th Detachment did not have a scout squad.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: All right. And tell me: What was the position held by Mr. Ilija Ceranic -- Cerianovic [phoen], sorry. Ilija Cerianovic?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the 4th Detachment, Ilija Cerianovic held no position.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Was he a member of the 4th Detachment? If you can't remember, just say "I can't remember."

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I have to go through 450 men now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Don't worry. Never mind. What about Dimitrije Ivanovski? Was he in the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: He's an ethnic Macedonian, isn't he?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: So this is this broad ethnic composition that you were explaining.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Fadil Topcagic was in the 4th Detachment, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Did he have a particular position?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: What about Mr. Ivanovski?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN ANTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was by the telephone at the command.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe that there are some matters to -- my colleagues would like to address the Chamber, and I was informed by Madam Registrar that it's about our time to stop the examination today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, with the witness, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can the witness be led out of the courtroom, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Maybe I will address first and then Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It has to do with Mr. Zaric and our trials on Monday. Mr. Zaric has a scheduled medical examination, but not with the problem that we have recently seen he does. But it has something to do with his optometrical examination, and it is scheduled for Monday at 11.00. That's the only term that this could be scheduled. And if he misses this examination, the next would be within the next three months. So he really doesn't feel that he should miss this examination. I discussed this issue with him and he's ready to waive his right of being present on Monday at the morning session until he completes his examination, and he was just asking for assistance that he should be brought immediately after this examination is completed in the courtroom. That's the only issue that we would like to raise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. I will ask the registry assistant to see that the relevant units are informed, that he will be brought to the courtroom immediately after his examination. Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have received the Prosecutor's response related to the last two statements, the 92 bis statements, D185/3 ID and 284/3 [as interpreted]. I would appreciate it if I could give a response too. Since the weekend is coming up --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
